item.title: Checking permissions in Forge: when to use asUser and asApp
item.description: A Forge app works perfectly when you test it as a Jira administrator. You switch to an ordinary project member, try the same action, and get a permission error. It can be tempting to change the API call from asUser() to asApp() and move on.

item.title: What to check before putting a Forge Remote backend into production
item.description: Suppose two customers use your reporting app. Both have a report numbered 42. The database keeps their records separate, but the remote backend caches a generated report under the key report:42.

item.title: What does an OWASP-based penetration test actually cover?
item.description: “We need an OWASP test before launch.” It’s a reasonable request, but the next conversation needs to be about the application: which users it serves, what they can do, and what would go wrong if a control failed.

item.title: Using AI during a penetration test
item.description: An AI tool reads an API specification and suggests a possible access-control problem. That might be a useful lead. Before it belongs in a penetration test report, someone needs to establish whether the endpoint exists in the tested version, whether the suspected behaviour is reachable, and what actually happens when it is tested.

item.title: Testing an AI assistant inside a Jira app
item.description: Imagine an assistant that summarises a Jira project and offers to create follow-up tasks. In a demo, it reads the issues, writes a helpful summary, and creates a task when asked. Everything appears to work.

item.title: Tusker
item.description: Your team has outgrown Excel and WhatsApp, but you’re not ready for enterprise software. What worked at 5 people breaks at 15. Spreadsheets, WhatsApp, quick calls - they got you here, but they can’t scale. Enterprise tools like Jira take months to set up and teams never adopt them.

item.title: A practical approach to application security
item.description:
Start with a shared scope

An assessment begins with the application and the question you need answered. Agree the assets, environments, roles, integrations, and business journeys in scope. Identify third-party dependencies, exclusions, and any constraints that affect coverage.
